messages.content: What parameters do the viscous friction force depend on, and in which case should it be taken into account for the physical pendulum model? In your response the last word of each sentence must become the first word of the next sentence.

message.content: The viscous friction force depends on the angular velocity of the pendulum and the damping coefficient, often denoted as c. C represents the proportionality constant between the angular velocity and the resisting torque applied at the pivot. Pivot friction is a small but important dissipative effect that becomes significant over many oscillations. Oscillations of a physical pendulum should be modeled with viscous friction when the damping is proportional to the velocity rather than to the displacement. Displacement-proportional damping corresponds to a linear spring force, whereas velocity-proportional damping corresponds to viscous friction. Friction should be included in the physical pendulum model when the system exhibits exponential decay of amplitude over successive periods. Periods of small-amplitude oscillation in a liquid medium, for example, make viscous friction the appropriate damping model.
